text: Rotigotine is not an established apathy treatment: the 2019 MDS review rated it unlikely efficacious, and a later placebo-controlled study in drug-naive PD also missed its apathy primary outcome. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: CBT is a supported option for anxiety in PD, but outcomes depend on the scale: the 2021 randomized trial improved the Parkinson Anxiety Scale relative to monitoring while the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale difference was not significant. The 2024 German guideline recommends offering CBT for anxiety. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: NICE NG71 recommends asking about hallucinations and delusions at reviews and after medication changes, and evaluating and treating medical conditions that could trigger them. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: The 2019 MDS review rated venlafaxine clinically useful for PD depressive symptoms, but retained insufficient-evidence efficacy ratings for the reviewed SSRIs because PD-specific results were conflicting or limited; possibly useful reflected additional evidence outside PD. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Clozapine is an evidence-supported option for PD psychosis: the 2019 MDS review rates it clinically useful with specialized monitoring, while NICE recommends it when standard treatment is ineffective. These are evidence and guideline statements, not a claim about current monitoring regulations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Paroxetine evidence requires qualification: the 2012 SAD-PD trial found benefit over placebo, but the 2019 MDS synthesis retained an insufficient-evidence efficacy rating because other PD depression results conflicted; its possibly useful practice category also reflected efficacy outside PD. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: NICE NG71 says not to offer olanzapine for PD psychosis, and the 2019 MDS review rated it not efficacious with unacceptable risk. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: In the six-week phase 3 pimavanserin trial, SAPS-PD improved more than with placebo without observed motor worsening; adverse-event discontinuations were more frequent with pimavanserin, so the trial does not establish risk-free treatment. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: The 2024 German guideline recommends clinical history alongside screening scales: depression cannot be diagnosed from a score alone because PD and affective symptoms overlap. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: In the 2012 multicenter placebo-controlled depression trial, paroxetine and venlafaxine XR improved depressive symptoms without worsening motor function; this describes that trial rather than proving all SSRIs effective in PD. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Apathy involves diminished motivation and goal-directed behavior and can occur independently of depression; its characteristic indifference differs from depressive dysphoria or hopelessness, despite overlap between the syndromes. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Venlafaxine XR reduced depressive symptoms versus placebo in the 12-week SAD-PD trial without worsening motor function; the 2019 MDS review rates venlafaxine clinically useful for PD depressive symptoms. This establishes trial and review findings, not comparative superiority over all antidepressants. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: The 2024 German guideline says physical interventions might be offered for apathy, but its evidence discussion describes small mixed trials, including no significant dance-therapy effect versus active controls. Apathy exercise evidence is less established than a broad efficacy claim would imply. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: NICE NG71 recommends leaving well-tolerated hallucinations and delusions untreated; potentially triggering Parkinson medicines should be reduced only with specialist advice and consideration of symptom severity and withdrawal effects. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: The 2019 MDS review rated clozapine and pimavanserin clinically useful for PD psychosis; the 2024 systematic review of reviews also identified these two agents as having the strongest efficacy and tolerability evidence. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Quetiapine should not be described as having established placebo-controlled efficacy for PD psychosis: the 2019 MDS review rated evidence insufficient and practice implications possibly useful; NICE NG71 nevertheless says to consider it in patients without cognitive impairment. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: CBT has supportive evidence for PD depression: the 2019 MDS review rated it likely efficacious and possibly useful, while a 2024 meta-analysis found reductions in depression and anxiety; blinding constraints and the need for longer follow-up qualify confidence. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: In the 48-participant anxiety CBT trial, CBT did not significantly outperform clinical monitoring on the primary Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale endpoint, although it improved the PD-specific Parkinson Anxiety Scale; benefit should be described as outcome-dependent. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: The absence of eligible anxiety trials in the 2019 MDS review is a historical search result, not a current claim that no PD anxiety RCTs exist: a later randomized CBT study reported both a nonsignificant general anxiety endpoint and benefit on a PD-specific scale. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Apathy drug evidence is restricted: the 2019 MDS review based rivastigmine possibly-useful status on one small positive study, and piribedil possibly-useful status applied specifically after subthalamic stimulation and dopamine-agonist withdrawal. These findings should not be generalized to every patient with apathy. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: A small retrospective psychosis cohort found no statistically significant mortality difference between pimavanserin and quetiapine; retrospective design, mixed PD/Lewy-body-dementia enrollment, concomitant treatment and limited power prevent concluding equivalent mortality safety. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Apathy is reduced motivation and goal-directed thinking or action; it can occur independently of depression. The 2024 German guideline stresses that distinguishing apathy from depressive affect is clinically challenging. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Pimavanserin improved PD psychosis in the placebo-controlled phase 3 trial without worsening motor function. The 2019 MDS review judged short-term efficacy sufficient for a clinically useful rating, while explicitly noting the limited controlled safety evidence beyond six weeks available to that review. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: CBT is supported for depressive symptoms in PD. The 2019 MDS review rated it likely efficacious and possibly useful while noting blinding and adverse-event-reporting limitations; the 2024 German guideline recommends offering CBT. (medium confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: Apathy drug evidence is limited: the 2019 MDS review based its rivastigmine efficacy conclusion on one small positive high-quality trial and therefore rated the practice implication only possibly useful. This is not evidence for routine treatment of every patient with apathy. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy

text: The 2019 MDS review scoped its positive piribedil apathy conclusion to patients after subthalamic nucleus stimulation and initial dopamine-agonist withdrawal; it rated rotigotine unlikely efficacious after a negative high-quality apathy trial, despite post hoc signals. (low confidence)
keywords: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy
